//: legacyWatch turns on polling instead of inotify.
Nodemon normally listens for kernel file-change events, which is cheap and
instant. Under WSL those events are not raised for files written from the
Windows side: copying through Explorer or saving from a Windows editor
changes the file on disk and tells the Linux kernel nothing. Nodemon sits
there believing nothing happened, and the server keeps serving the old
code with no error to suggest otherwise.
Polling checks the files on a timer instead, so it notices a change however
the file arrived. It costs a little CPU, which on a project this size is
